sources.title: Historical Basemaps: Sri Lanka index and five snapshots
sources.note: Local index and decoded 1945, 1960, 1994, 2000 and 2010 polygon checks; see identities.json and geometry-checks.json.

sources.title: Parliament of Sri Lanka: Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference bulletin, 9 September 2012
sources.note: Direct PDF, human page 2, The Parliamentary System of Government; constitutional transitions in 1948, 1972 and 1978.

sources.title: Constitution of Sri Lanka: English revised edition, 2023
sources.note: Direct PDF. Article 18 and Article 19, printed page 11, human PDF page 35. Budget combined with Sinhala edition.

sources.title: Constitution of Sri Lanka: Sinhala revised edition, 2023
sources.note: Official PDF downloaded and first page rendered and visually read. Title sample; edition revised through 31 October 2022, published 2023. Budget combined with English edition.

sources.title: Parliament of Sri Lanka: Women in Parliament, Who we are
sources.note: Indexed original history: Sirimavo Bandaranaike became the first female head of government on 21 July 1960. Only historical claim used; no current officeholder count.

sources.title: UNHCR: Sri Lanka makes citizens out of stateless tea pickers, 7 October 2004
sources.note: Direct original story by Chetani Priyanga Wijetunga. October 2003 law and December mobile campaign, Appu Kullamma testimony.

sources.title: Human Rights Watch: World Report 2025, Sri Lanka, events of 2024
sources.note: Direct original report, opening and Accountability and Justice sections. War dates, combatants, grave violations by both sides and 2024 elections.

sources.title: UN Geneva: Sri Lanka has an opportunity to break with past impunity, 13 August 2025
sources.note: Direct Spanish UN account of human rights report; accountability, occupied land and relatives seeking truth. Dated assessment, not a claim of completed reforms.

sources.title: UNHCR helps resolve land issues in Sri Lanka’s north, November 2012
sources.note: Indexed original UNHCR story published 23 November 2012, dateline 6 November. Missing ownership documents and return after May 2009.

sources.title: World Bank: Sri Lanka Development Update, April 2025
sources.note: Indexed original publication summary dated 23 April 2025. Default and contraction, 2024 growth and household purchasing power. No numeric poverty threshold repeated.

sources.title: World Bank Statement on Sri Lanka, 28 July 2022
sources.note: Indexed original statement, reallocated resources for essential medicines, cooking gas, fertilizer, school meals and transfers.

sources.title: Sri Lanka Tourism: Food range
sources.note: Indexed original national tourism guide, checked September 2026; Kiribath, Imbul Kiribath and Kokis sections. Contemporary descriptive source, not a claim that every family follows the same customs.

sources.title: UNESCO: Rūkada Nātya, traditional string puppet drama in Sri Lanka, inscribed 2018
sources.note: Indexed original entry: Gamwari family groups, Ambalangoda, Balapitiya and Mirissa; scripts, carving, music and community performance.

sources.title: UNESCO: Traditional craftsmanship of making Dumbara Ratā Kalāla, nomination for 2021 inscription
sources.note: Indexed original nomination, page 2 community and location sections; Kinnara communities, Kalāsirigama and Alōkagama.

sources.title: World Bank: SABER School Feeding, Sri Lanka Country Report 2015
sources.note: Indexed original report, Education and Health in Sri Lanka section: free education, textbooks, uniform fabric, medical services, subsidized transport, scholarships and selected-school meals.

sources.title: UNICEF: Building Strong Foundations, 24 January 2025
sources.note: Direct original story by Pramitha Herath, Chandralatha and Pipena Kekulu Preschool; original lack of toilets and water, new November 2024 building. New toilet installation is not individually specified and is not claimed.

sources.title: UNICEF: Breaking taboos and empowering communities, 3 June 2024
sources.note: Direct original story by Lakna Paranamanna; Fasmila Begum and Chanidu Himasaw, health education and school assemblies.

sources.title: WHO certifies Sri Lanka malaria-free, 5 September 2016
sources.note: Direct WHO announcement; 1990s strategy change, mobile clinics, surveillance, community engagement and elimination certification.

sources.title: WHO: Driven to end malaria, ten years of success for Sri Lanka, 24 April 2026
sources.note: Indexed original WHO retrospective; imported cases and mosquito vectors persist, requiring continued surveillance.

sources.title: Central Bank of Sri Lanka: Current note series
sources.note: Direct official text descriptions of Rs.20 and Rs.100 note designs. No claim based on an independently inspected banknote image.

proposedOverrides.name: Sri Lanka
proposedOverrides.summary: Modern Sri Lanka, with the atlas’s final colonial years clearly distinguished from independence and the republic.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct modern card; no shared association with Ceylon, Kandy, Simhala or Sinhalese kingdoms.
batchIdentityNotes.map: Indexed 1945 to present. Five coarse island snapshots miss several coastal city coordinates; not civil-war control maps.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Sinhala constitution title, 2023 printed revised edition, visually verified; English/Sinhala editions counted as one work.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: Reports retain dates; no universal toilet access, uniform culture or completed postwar justice asserted. Preschool source verifies former sanitation deficiencies but does not itemize a new toilet. Last phase ends exclusively in 2027 to include evidence dated 2026, not as a predicted state ending.
